Use when starting testing on a feature or a codebase, when asked for a test plan or why coverage sits where it does, or when a suite is large and still missing bugs. Not for writing the tests themselves, and not for proving a finished change works.

skills.use_when: A system's shape is being designed or changed — new service, integration, tenancy model, uploads, payments or auth — and someone needs to know which few things are actually worth defending.
skills.not_for: Finding defects in existing code (secure-code-review), enumerating web bug classes in a codebase (owasp-web), compliance questionnaires, or responding to a live incident.
skills.name: threat-modeling
skills.summary: A system's shape is being designed or changed — new service, integration, tenancy model, uploads, payments or auth — and someone needs to know which few things are actually worth defending.
skills.description: Work out what is actually worth defending in this system — the trust boundaries data crosses, the assets behind them, what an attacker can already do, and the small number of threats that justify a control. Use when designing or changing a system's shape, before building auth, payments, uploads, file sharing or multi-tenancy, when adding an integration that crosses a boundary, or when asked whether a design is safe. Not for finding bugs in code that already exists (that is secure-code-review), not a compliance questionnaire, and not incident response.

skills.use_when: A tool or function an LLM calls is being added or reshaped, or an agent is selecting the wrong tool, passing malformed arguments, looping, or stalling after a call.
skills.not_for: Building or integrating the MCP server that hosts the tools (mcp-design), constraining a model's final answer to a schema (structured-output), general prompt wording, or internal functions no model invokes.
skills.name: tool-design
skills.summary: A tool or function an LLM calls is being added or reshaped, or an agent is selecting the wrong tool, passing malformed arguments, looping, or stalling after a call.
skills.description: Design the tools a model calls — names, parameter shapes, what a result returns, and error text written as an instruction the model can act on. Use when adding or reshaping a tool or function an LLM invokes, when an agent keeps calling the wrong tool or passing malformed arguments, or when reviewing a tool surface someone else defined. Not for building the MCP server that hosts the tools (mcp-design), not for forcing a model's final answer into a schema (structured-output), and not for prompt wording outside the tool definition.

skills.use_when: An interface already exists and someone needs to know what is wrong with it, ranked and concrete enough to act on.
skills.not_for: Proving a change renders and functions (browser-verification), setting a visual direction where none exists (frontend-design), or a formal accessibility conformance audit.
skills.name: ui-audit
skills.summary: An interface already exists and someone needs to know what is wrong with it, ranked and concrete enough to act on.
skills.description: Review an existing interface and return ranked, concrete findings — each with its location, the user consequence, and a specific fix — instead of taste notes. Use when asked to critique, audit or review a screen or flow, when someone's UI work needs judging, or when an interface "feels off" and the problem needs naming. Not for proving a change renders and functions, not for inventing a new visual direction, and not for an accessibility conformance audit, which is its own discipline.

skills.use_when: Interface strings are being written, reviewed or repaired — labels, errors, empty states, confirmations, form hints — or a control's wording is causing hesitation.
skills.not_for: Marketing and landing-page copy, documentation and release notes, or deciding layout and visual treatment (ui-design).
skills.name: ux-writing
skills.summary: Interface strings are being written, reviewed or repaired — labels, errors, empty states, confirmations, form hints — or a control's wording is causing hesitation.
skills.description: Write or repair the words inside an interface — button labels, empty states, error messages, confirmation dialogs, form hints, success and loading text — so a reader knows what just happened and what to do next. Use when a screen's copy is being written or reviewed, when an error says something unhelpful, when a confirmation is vague about what it will do, or when users hesitate at a control. Not for marketing or landing-page copy, not for documentation, and not for deciding layout or visual design.

skills.use_when: A change affects appearance and is about to be called done, or a screenshot-comparison result is about to be trusted as proof.
skills.not_for: A single rendered check of one change (browser-verification), judging whether a design is good (ui-audit), or behaviour with no visual surface.
skills.name: visual-verification
skills.summary: A change affects appearance and is about to be called done, or a screenshot-comparison result is about to be trusted as proof.
skills.description: Prove a UI looks right across every state and viewport it has to survive — enumerate the state matrix, make captures deterministic, compare against a baseline captured the same way, and triage every diff. Use before calling a visual change, a style refactor or a redesign done, when running or trusting a screenshot-comparison suite, and when asked whether a screen still looks correct. Not for judging whether a design is good, not for proving controls actually work, and never on its own sufficient to call a page verified.

skills.use_when: A webhook endpoint is being built, integrated or debugged, or the service has to deliver events to external consumers.
skills.not_for: Internal queue or event-bus consumers with no HTTP trust boundary, general outbound API retry policy (idempotency-and-retries), and ordinary request/response endpoint design (api-design).
skills.name: webhooks
skills.summary: A webhook endpoint is being built, integrated or debugged, or the service has to deliver events to external consumers.
skills.description: Receive or send HTTP webhooks correctly — signature verification on the raw body, fast acknowledgement, deduplication, out-of-order handling, retry and dead-letter behaviour, and the delivery contract a consumer needs. Use when adding or debugging a webhook endpoint, when integrating a provider's events, or when your own service has to notify others of changes. Not for internal queue or event-bus messages that never cross an HTTP boundary, and not for general outbound API retry policy.
